To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
ZN/ST (ZnNb2O6–SrTiO3) stacked resonators with zero τf have the potential for application in temperature stable microwave devices.
a temperature-stable ZnNb2O _{6} -SrTiO _{3} (ZN/ST)-stacked resonator with τ _{f}  = 0 ppm/°C was achieved for 8.56 wt% ST.
microwave dielectric properties of a ZN/ ST stacked resonator can be adjusted by varying the volume percentage of SrTiO3.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new method to obtain a zero τf for a ZN/SrTiO3 stacked resonator.
the dielectric properties of ZN/ST resonators with a wide range of ST volume percentages.
the development of a microwave dielectric resonator with zero τf.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the dielectric properties of the stacked resonator are determined by the properties of the constituent resonators.
the microwave dielectric properties of the ZN/ST system can be tuned by varying ST content.
the microwave dielectric properties of ZN/ST resonators can be tuned by adjusting the volume percentages of ST.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ZN/ST system can be considered as one of the most promising candidates for microwave dielectric applications.
the microwave dielectric properties of the ZN/ST system are very sensitive to the ST content.
the ZN/ST resonators have the potential of being used as temperature-stable resonators in the X-band.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the dielectric properties of the stacked resonator can be controlled by changing the volume percentage of SrTiO3.
the dielectric properties of the stacked resonator can be tuned by adjusting the volume fraction of the secondary phase.
the microwave dielectric properties of the ZN/ST system can be tailored by adjusting the volume ratio of ST, and the microwave dielectric resonators with zero τf and εr = 24.6 are obtained.
